name: PropertyGrid
description:
A label/value editor driven by a row schema: each item's `type` picks
the control (TextField, NumberField, Select, Switch, TextArea, or a
`custom` render), and rows are divided with Separator. The label
column auto-sizes to the longest label via CSS Grid's max-content,
capped by maxLabelWidth. Label and field always stay side by side on
the same row: a long label wraps within its own column rather than
pushing the field down or being ellipsised.
whenToUse: Viewing and editing an object’s properties in a compact two-column list: an inspector panel, a resource’s settings, a selected item’s details.
`readOnly` items for values people see but can’t change.

whenNotToUse.text: A form people fill once (sign-up, checkout)
Many records with the same fields

anatomy.description: sized to the longest label, capped by `maxLabelWidth`; long labels wrap.
control per `type`: text, number, select, switch, textarea, custom.
separated by a Separator; description under the control.

do.caption: An object’s properties, scanned and tweaked in place.

dont.caption: A sign-up form as a grid: labels squeezed left, no room for help or errors — stack it instead.

a11y: Each label is a real label for its control; the grid is not a table to screen readers.
Read-only values render as plain text (a read-only switch as a disabled switch), so they read and copy like any text.

props.name: maxLabelWidth
props.description: Cap on the label column (any CSS length). The column is still sized to the longest label; this only moves the ceiling past which labels ellipsise.
